chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Faddal from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from some of our companions who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells a sale for more than he buys, and he said, 'It is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods for more than the purchase price in Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases and sales, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the validity of markup in trade, reflecting the permissibility of profit in commercial transactions. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that as long as there is no deception or riba (usury), the difference between purchase and selling price is a legitimate gain. This ruling provides a foundational basis for modern retail and wholesale pricing strategies in Islamic finance.
